segments: Chronography of Bar Hebraeus.
the Turks entered,
the king of the Iberians seized the clisuras (mountain passes),
and destroyed many of them.
And Joscelin the Frank took the region of Gūbōs captive.
And in the year 516 [AH],
[when] his wife [died],
and he took as a second wife the daughter of Roger, the lord of Antioch,
and he wished to bring her to Edessa,
Balak set an ambush for her,
and captured her and brought her to Būlā.
And Michael the Armenian, when he was defeated by the Turks,
gave Gargar to King Baldwin,
and took for himself a place in his territory.
And in the year 517 [AH],
[1123 AD] Ibn al-Shahrazūrī, the judge of Mosul, came to Baghdad,
and presented to the Caliph five thousand dinars,
and he was given authority over the whole western side of the Tigris,
from Mosul as far as Basra.
And in the year 1434
of the Greeks [1123 AD],
while the Franks were encamped on the river Sangas (Sanjah),
the ambush of Balak, the Turkish emir, fell upon them.
And they attacked the camp of the Franks,
and captured King Baldwin on the Wednesday of White Week.
Joscelin, however, and Count Galeran prepared all summer to engage the Turks;
and when they met them in the month of Elul, the Franks were likewise broken,
and Joscelin and Galeran were captured on the eve of the Feast of the Cross.
And all three of them together Balak imprisoned in the fortress of Zaid in a pit.
Then certain Armenian men,
laborers who were in the city,
when they learned that there were few [guards] in the fortress,
assembled at the gate making a pretext about their wages.
And they sprang suddenly and seized the swords that were there,
and killed the Turkish guards.
And they ran to the pit,
and brought out King Baldwin, Joscelin, and Galeran.
And they killed the Arabs (Muslims),
and took possession of the fortress of Zaid,
which is Kharput (Kharpirt).
And Joscelin took counsel,
and went out at night with an Armenian,
to go and bring an army of the Franks,
so that, if possible,
they might hold the fortress,
and if not,
they might take away the king.
